clue.text: Hides family on board

indicators.note: being on board a vessel puts the family between the ship's letters, so 'on' wraps them round

parts.note: on board a steamship, abbreviated SS, a crossword convention
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: Animal hides belonging to a family are carried aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is a crossword convention for putting something inside SS, the abbreviation for steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal pelts are called both hides and skins.

clue.text: Master is east of craft

parts.note: an expert is a master of a subject
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A master craftsman is placed to the east of a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like a boat in the surface; it is skill, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Craft as a noun means skill, and expertise is specialist skill.

clue.text: Value of tar-the last to join ship?

definitions.text: Value of tar-the last to join ship?

parts.words: Value of tar-the last to join ship?
parts.note: points to the proverb about spoiling the ship for a tiny amount's worth of tar, the final item loaded

explanation.surface: Asking what the tar is worth, the last thing put aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'don't spoil the ship for a ha'porth of tar' warns against skimping on the last small cost; a halfpenny was an old British coin worth half a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: The amount bought for an old half-penny coin is a tiny value, the proverb's quantity of tar.

clue.text: First pair getting the ball rolling

explanation.surface: The first two batsmen start the cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the first pair of batsmen are the openers; openers are also remarks or moves that start things going.

clue.text: Butcher's short sight?

explanation.surface: A butcher's shop seen only briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher's' is Cockney rhyming slang: butcher's hook means look.
explanation.definitionFit: A butcher's is a quick look in rhyming slang, and a brief view is a short sight.

clue.text: Alliance concealed by Pablo Casals

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of the cellist's name, hidden across its two words

explanation.surface: A political alliance kept secret by the Spanish cellist Pablo Casals.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is a group of nations or parties joined in a common cause.

clue.text: Wood of bow in left hand

indicators.note: the bow's shape is set between the two abbreviations, so 'in' places it inside them

parts.note: a bow is curved, an arc

explanation.surface: An archer's wooden bow held in the left hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Larch is a conifer whose timber is used as wood.

clue.text: Furrow following wagon round

indicators.note: the furrow word comes after the wagon word in the answer

parts.note: a cart is a wagon
in ridge-and-furrow ploughing the soil is turned into ridges, so a furrow is also taken as a ridge or groove

explanation.surface: A furrow ploughed behind a wagon going round a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like a direction; it is the definition, a single shot of ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: A round is one unit of ammunition, a bullet in its casing.

clue.text: Sublime, neat non-tumble underthings

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Sublime, neat non-tumble underthings (14)': NEAT NON TUMBLE gives a second T and lacks the I and S the answer needs; no word supplies them, and the fix is beyond an OCR slip.

clue.text: I am getting ahead of beat, in sudden whim

indicators.note: the contraction is placed in front of the beat word

parts.note: contracted to I'M
a pulse is a beat

explanation.surface: Getting in front of the rhythm on a sudden whim.
explanation.definitionFit: An impulse is a sudden urge to act.

clue.text: He turns his back on wild region to the right

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of region run loose

explanation.surface: A man who turns away from a wild region lying to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He turns his back on' reads as a description of an action, but it is a noun phrase for a person who snubs; 'wild' is the anagram signal and 'to the right' adds R at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pays no attention to another snubs them, giving them the cold shoulder.

clue.text: Where litter is left to fight a great deal

parts.note: a scrap is a fight
a heap is a large amount

explanation.surface: Fighting over a great deal of litter left lying around.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubbish dump where discarded things are thrown.

clue.text: Sheer turmoil here in Surrey

indicators.note: turmoil is disorder, so the letters of sheer are thrown about

explanation.surface: Utter turmoil in a quiet Surrey town.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county south-west of London; ESHER is one of its towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Esher is a town in the county of Surrey.

clue.text: Prison holding short Irish terrier

indicators.note: the prison word contains the Irish abbreviation

parts.note: can is slang for prison
IR is the abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: A jail holding a small Irish terrier.
explanation.walkthrough: CAN is American slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The cairn is a small Scottish breed of terrier dog.

clue.text: Rev up in glen, my car is mobile

indicators.note: something mobile moves about, so these letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: Revving the engine in a glen where my car is on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rev up' reads as revving an engine; 'Rev' alone is the definition, short for Reverend.
explanation.definitionFit: Rev is short for Reverend, the title of a minister of the church.

clue.text: Does one retain our worry-beads?

parts.note: worry-beads read as drops of perspiration brought on by worry, held back by a strip of cloth round the head

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone keeps hold of our string of worry-beads.
explanation.walkthrough: Worry-beads are a string of beads fingered to calm nerves; here they are beads of sweat from worrying.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip worn round the forehead or wrist soaks up perspiration.

clue.text: Affluence of a Chelsea Ball?

parts.note: a Chelsea bun is a type of currant bun
a ball is a dance

explanation.surface: Wealth on display at a society ball in Chelsea.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea is a wealthy London district, but here it is a Chelsea bun, a spiralled currant bun.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluence is plenty, and abundance means a great plenty.

clue.text: All Souls?

parts.note: souls as people: all of them

explanation.surface: A reference to All Souls, the Oxford college or the feast day.
explanation.walkthrough: All Souls suggests the Oxford college or the feast day, but souls are simply people.
explanation.definitionFit: Souls means people, so all souls is every person.

clue.text: Moor to return greeting

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the little word is read backwards

parts.note: hello is a greeting

explanation.surface: Returning a greeting on the moor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moor' looks like open heathland; it is Shakespeare's Moor of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragic hero is a Moorish general of Venice.

clue.text: Disease of horse and chicken soon to begin

parts.note: chicken and yellow both mean cowardly

indicators.note: only the beginning of the word soon is used

explanation.surface: A horse and a chicken that will soon fall ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellows is jaundice in horses and other animals.

clue.text: Unfertilized seed united in love, possibly

indicators.note: the united letter is set inside the jumbled love
possibly says the letters of love could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A seed not yet fertilized, united in love perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges LOVE as OVLE; 'in' puts U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovule is the structure in a plant that becomes a seed after fertilization.

clue.text: Appetite got us in a bad way

indicators.note: in a bad way means in poor shape, so the letters are in disorder

explanation.surface: Our appetite has left us feeling ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty enjoyment, a keen relish.

clue.text: Salary- Archimedes' idea?

explanation.surface: Asking whether paying wages was the Greek inventor's idea.
explanation.walkthrough: SCREW is old British slang for wages; the Archimedes screw is a water-raising device credited to him.
explanation.definitionFit: Screw is slang for pay, and the Archimedean screw is a pump invented by the Greek mathematician.

clue.text: Also call round for Rembrandt, say

indicators.note: the shout wraps round the joining word

parts.note: holler means call out
and means also

explanation.surface: Also calling out on behalf of the painter Rembrandt.
explanation.definitionFit: Rembrandt was Dutch, a native of the Netherlands.

clue.text: Somewhere to settle in kangaroo's territory

indicators.note: the answer sits in the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A place to settle in the kangaroo's home range.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a perch where birds settle to rest.

clue.text: A mitral disorder of a husband

indicators.note: a disorder suggests the letters are disarranged

explanation.surface: A heart-valve disorder suffered by someone's husband.
explanation.walkthrough: The mitral is a heart valve; the surface reads as a medical condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital means relating to marriage, the husband and wife bond.

clue.text: Centre of corn earth-circle (One of 4 in AYLI)

indicators.note: only the central letters of corn are used

parts.note: land is earth
a circle is shaped like O

explanation.surface: A crop circle in the middle of a cornfield.
explanation.walkthrough: AYLI is Shakespeare's As You Like It, which ends with four couples marrying; 4 is not the cross-reference to 4-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando is the hero of As You Like It, one of the four bridegrooms at the play's end.

clue.text: All-points bulletin

parts.note: north is one compass point, N
east, E
west, W
south, S

explanation.surface: A police all-points bulletin.
explanation.walkthrough: An all-points bulletin is a police alert; here 'All-points' gives all four compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: A news bulletin is a broadcast report.

clue.text: Swarming insects not true to type?

indicators.note: swarming insects move about in a mass, so the letters mill around

explanation.surface: Swarming insects that do not behave as expected.
explanation.definitionFit: Consistent means unchanging, always behaving the same way.
